questions.q: What event in 1971 marked the definitive end of the Bretton Woods system of fixed exchange rates?
questions.a: The correct answer is: US President Richard Nixon's unilateral suspension of the dollar's convertibility into gold (the "Nixon Shock") on 15 August 1971. A wrong answer such as "the 1973 oil crisis" or "the formation of the WTO" reveals the student confuses the monetary trigger with later consequences or institutional developments, and does not grasp that the collapse of the gold-dollar anchor preceded the oil shocks and floating rates.

questions.q: Why did developing countries (Group of 77) demand a New International Economic Order (NIEO) in the 1970s? Explain two core demands.
questions.a: Developing countries demanded NIEO because they faced deteriorating terms of trade, debt burdens, and lack of technology transfer while Western MNCs controlled their resources. Two core demands: (1) sovereign control over natural resources and nationalisation rights without unfair compensation; (2) regulated commodity prices and technology transfer on favourable terms. A wrong answer focusing only on "more aid" or "lower tariffs" misses the structural critique — NIEO sought to rewrite the rules of ownership, pricing, and technology, not just increase aid flows.

questions.q: A multinational corporation (MNC) designs a product in the USA, sources raw materials from Chile, manufactures components in Vietnam and Mexico, assembles in China, and sells globally. Which two post-1970s developments made this fragmented production network possible?
questions.a: The two key developments: (1) Revolution in transport (containerisation, larger cargo ships) drastically lowering shipping costs and time; (2) Revolution in communication (satellites, fibre optics, later internet) enabling real-time coordination of complex supply chains across continents. A wrong answer citing "the Bretton Woods system" or "colonial trade routes" shows the student cannot distinguish the pre-1970s framework from the technological and policy shifts that enabled modern global value chains.

questions.q: Compare the role of the IMF and World Bank under Bretton Woods (1944–1971) with their role after the 1980s debt crisis. How did their policy conditionalities change?
questions.a: Under Bretton Woods, the IMF provided short-term balance-of-payments support to maintain fixed exchange rates; the World Bank funded reconstruction and development projects. After the 1980s debt crisis, both institutions imposed Structural Adjustment Programmes (SAPs) — requiring deregulation, privatisation, fiscal austerity, and trade liberalisation as loan conditions — shifting from stability-focused lending to enforcing neoliberal policy reforms. A wrong answer stating "their role remained the same" or "they started giving more grants" fails to recognise the pivotal ideological shift toward the Washington Consensus.

questions.q: Evaluate the statement: "The New International Economic Order (NIEO) failed completely because developing countries lacked unity and the West refused all concessions." Provide a nuanced judgment with evidence.
questions.a: The statement is partially correct but oversimplified. NIEO did not achieve its major goals (commodity price stabilisation, binding technology transfer codes, reform of IMF voting) due to Western opposition (veto power in IMF/World Bank, refusal to negotiate binding codes) and divisions within G77 (oil exporters vs. non-oil exporters). However, it secured some gains: the UN Declaration on the Right to Development (1986), the Common Fund for Commodities (1989), and greater Southern voice in UNCTAD. A wrong answer calling it a "total success" or "total failure" lacks the balanced evaluation required for board exam competency questions.

questions.q: Construct a timeline with 5 key events (1971–1995) that trace the shift from the collapse of Bretton Woods to the establishment of the WTO, showing how each event advanced economic globalisation.
questions.a: A strong timeline includes: (1) 1971: Nixon ends dollar-gold convertibility → floating exchange rates; (2) 1973: First oil shock → petrodollar recycling, Third World debt buildup; (3) 1982: Mexican debt crisis → IMF structural adjustment programmes spread; (4) 1986: Uruguay Round of GATT negotiations begins → expands trade rules to services, IP, agriculture; (5) 1995: WTO established → enforceable dispute settlement, binding global trade rules. A poor timeline lists unrelated events (e.g., "fall of Berlin Wall" without linking to economic integration) or misses the causal chain from monetary collapse to trade institutionalisation.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: ______ and the New International Economic Order (NIEO) refers to the post-1970s phase of accelerated economic integration driven by multinational corporations (MNCs), technological revolutions in transport and communication, and the demands of developing nations (Group of 77) for a fairer global economic system — including sovereign control over natural resources, technology transfer, and reform of international trade rules — after the collapse of the Bretton Woods fixed exchange rate system in 1971.

Fill in the blank: Imagine you are buying a smartphone assembled in China, with chips from ______, software from the USA, and rare earth minerals from Africa — all coordinated by a company headquartered in California.
Fill in the blank: The key insight: globalisation after ______ was not inevitable; it was shaped by policy choices, corporate strategies, and power struggles between the Global North and South.
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student can explain how the end of Bretton Woods, the rise of MNCs, and the NIEO demands collectively reshaped the global economy, and can evaluate why developing countries' demands for a New International Economic Order were only partially met.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Imagine you are buying a smartphone assembled in China, with chips from Taiwan, software from the USA, and rare earth minerals from Africa — all coordinated by a company ______ in California.
